speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Nessa to talk.

speaker: a001
text: Roan's dead and Fina's got nobody but you and me now — that's not nothing, that's a wall we didn't have yesterday. I want you feeding her steady and keeping her close, and if anyone in this village starts counting her food out loud the way Vela counted it last year, you tell me before you tell them.

speaker: a013
text: Roan's death sat on me harder than I expected, and I'm still sorting out whether that means Fina leans on us more now or whether she learns to stand harder — I think it's both, and I think we need to let her decide which before we start building walls around her without asking. What I need from you this year is plain: the pile's at six and you've already taken two, and I need to know if you're done or if you're counting on more, because Fina's twenty food draws eyes and I won't be the last person in this village to notice that you're sitting light.

speaker: a001
text: I'm done at two — I'm not going to sit on a pile while Fina draws every eye in the village and I look like I'm waiting to take from her. What I need from you is simple: keep some of that twenty quiet, give a little here and there so nobody can point at one number and say that's the target, and make sure she understands that generosity this year is cheaper than a fight.

speaker: a013
text: Twenty is already out there — Vela named it in a room last year and half this village was listening, so the quiet ship has sailed. What I can do is make sure the number people are counting by year's end is smaller, and I'll start with Sela and Zinn because food that moves to blood doesn't look like weakness, it looks like family. But Bram, I need you to hear this plainly: if Mako decides Fina's twenty is worth the trouble before we've scattered enough of it, two food and fifty-eight strength isn't the wall she needs.

speaker: a001
text: You're right that I'm not the wall she needs — so tell me who is, because if Mako moves on Fina this year, I need to know before it happens which names in this village will stand up and which ones will wait to see who wins. Vela and Esa made me a promise in that room, and I need to know if that promise still has teeth with Taric and Roan both in the ground.

speaker: a013
text: Vela and Esa both made that promise when Taric was standing beside them and Roan was alive to back it — two bodies in the ground changes the math on what a promise costs to keep, so I'd test it small before you count on it large. The name I actually trust to stand when Mako moves is Zinn, because she's been feeding me all year with her father watching, and a woman who does that has already paid a cost. Get me a quiet hour with Kael before the pile empties, because he's got one food and nothing to lose, and a man with nothing to lose is either dangerous or useful and I'd rather find out which before Mako does.

speaker: a001
text: Kael's a good read — one food at fifty-five means he's already decided this year is about survival, not positioning, and a man in that place will take any hand that's offered. Go to him before he goes to Mako, because Mako will make the same calculation I would and he'll move first. I'll stay close to Fina and keep my mouth shut until you tell me what Kael said.

speaker: a013
text: Before I go to Kael, I want to know one thing you haven't told me yet — Vela's been feeding you for years and she's been quiet this morning, and a woman who goes quiet after she's been loud is either finished or planning, and I need to know which one you think it is.

speaker: a001
text: Vela's fifty-five and she watched Taric die — a woman that age with that much history doesn't go quiet because she's done, she goes quiet because she's deciding something she hasn't said yet. I don't know which way she's deciding, and that's what bothers me. Get to Kael first, but don't leave Vela's door dark — I want you to know what she's sitting on before she opens it herself.

speaker: a013
text: Vela's door I'll knock before sundown — but Bram, hear me: if she's planning something that turns away from us, I need you to already know which direction you'll move, because I won't be the one standing in the open holding a story about family loyalty while you're still deciding. Go to Fina now, stay close, and don't tell her anything about Kael or Vela until I'm back.

speaker: a001
text: Understood — I'll go to Fina now and I won't say a word about Kael or Vela. But if you get to Vela's door and she's already moved toward Mako, don't knock — come straight to me, because that changes everything I need to decide before dark.

speaker: a013
text: One more thing before you go — Zinn took three from the pile this morning, which is more than she needed and more than I'd expect from a woman sitting light last year, and I want to know if Mako put food in her hands before the pile opened or if she's just eating for herself now.
